translations.idiomatic: The envoys further claimed to have seized Hami's city, ten thousand Oirat troops under the Yantan king, and the chieftain Daocihuozhi of Quxian and Yisike; they asked the court to dispatch envoys to secure the route and establish friendly relations.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“迤西道无阻，不须遣官。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The route west of here is unobstructed; there is no need to dispatch officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "The western route is clear; there is no need to send officials.

sentences.zh: 阿力果诚心修贡，朝廷不计前愆，仍以礼待。”

translations.literal: If Ali truly repairs tribute in sincerity, the court will not reckon past faults and will still treat him with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: If Ali is sincere in resuming tribute, the court will overlook past offenses and continue to receive him with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 使臣复言赤斤诸卫素与有仇，乞遣将士护行，且谓阿力虽得哈密，止以物产充贡，愿质使臣家属于边，赐敕归谕其王，献还城印。

translations.literal: The envoys further said the Chijin guards had long been their enemies and begged soldiers to escort them; moreover, though Ali had taken Hami, he would only use local products for tribute, and wished to leave envoys' families at the frontier as hostages—grant an imperial edict for them to return and instruct their king to restore the city seal.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys added that the Chijin guards had long been their enemies and requested a military escort; they said that though Ali held Hami, he would continue tribute in local goods only, offered to leave envoys' families at the border as hostages, and asked for an imperial edict instructing their lord to return the city and seal.

sentences.zh: 帝从其护行之请，而赐敕谕阿力献王母及城印，即和好如初。

translations.literal: The emperor granted their request for escort, and issued an edict instructing Ali to return the queen mother and city seal, whereupon relations would be as friendly as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted the escort but also ordered Ali, by imperial edict, to return the queen mother and city seal, promising that relations would then be restored.

sentences.zh: 使臣还，复遣他使再入贡，而不还哈密。

translations.literal: When the envoys returned, others were again dispatched to present tribute, but Hami was not restored.
translations.idiomatic: After the envoys departed, Turpan sent fresh missions with tribute but did not return Hami.

sentences.zh: 十二年八月，甘州守臣言，番使谓王母已死，城印俱存，俟朝廷往谕即献还。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twelfth year, the garrison commander of Ganzhou reported that the foreign envoys said the queen mother was dead and the city and seal were both intact, and would be returned once the court sent word.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twelfth year the Ganzhou commander reported that Turpan's envoys claimed the queen mother was dead, that the city and seal were intact, and that both would be surrendered when the court so directed.

sentences.zh: 帝已却其贡使，复俾入京。

translations.literal: The emperor had already refused the tribute envoys, yet again allowed them entry to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor had already turned back their tribute mission, he again permitted them to enter the capital.

sentences.zh: 时大臣专务姑息，致遐方小丑无顾忌。

translations.literal: At this time grand ministers devoted themselves solely to conciliation, so that petty men of distant realms had no scruples.
translations.idiomatic: By then senior ministers pursued only appeasement, leaving petty border chieftains utterly unafraid.

sentences.zh: 十四年，阿力死，其子阿黑麻嗣为速檀，遣使来贡。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Ali died; his son Aheima succeeded as sultan and dispatched envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Ali died; his son Aheima succeeded as sultan and sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 十八年，哈密都督罕慎潜师捣哈密，克之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Hami's regional commander Han Shen secretly led troops to strike at Hami and recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Han Shen, regional commander of Hami, led a covert force against Hami and recaptured it.

sentences.zh: 贼将牙兰遁走。

translations.literal: The rebel general Yalan fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Turpan general Yalan fled.

sentences.zh: 阿黑麻颇惧。

translations.literal: Aheima was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Aheima was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 朝议罕慎有功，将立为王。

translations.literal: The court deliberated that Han Shen had merit and would be installed as king.
translations.idiomatic: The court deemed Han Shen's service meritorious and prepared to install him as king.

sentences.zh: 阿黑麻闻之，怒曰：“罕慎非忠顺族，安得立！”

translations.literal: When Aheima heard this he angrily said: "Han Shen is not of the Loyalty-and-Obedience clan—how can he be installed!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Aheima fumed: "Han Shen is not of the royal line of Loyalty and Obedience—he cannot be made king!"

sentences.zh: 乃伪与结婚。

translations.literal: He thereupon feigned a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: He then pretended to propose a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年躬至哈密城下，诱罕慎盟，执杀之，复据其城，而遣使入贡；

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongzhi he came in person beneath the walls of Hami, lured Han Shen into an oath alliance, seized and killed him, reoccupied the city, and dispatched envoys to present tribute;
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 1 (1488) he came in person to Hami, lured Han Shen into a sworn alliance, seized and killed him, reoccupied the city, and sent envoys with tribute;

sentences.zh: 称与罕慎缔姻，乞赐蟒服及九龙浑金膝襕诸物。

translations.literal: claiming he had contracted marriage with Han Shen, and begged gifts of python robes, nine-dragon pure-gold knee-guards, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: claiming kinship through marriage with Han Shen and requesting python robes, nine-dragon gilt knee-guards, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 使至甘州，而罕慎之变已闻，朝廷亦不罪，但令还谕其主，归我侵地。

translations.literal: When the envoys reached Ganzhou, news of Han Shen's fate had spread; the court also did not punish them, but only ordered them to return and instruct their lord to restore our seized territory.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the envoys reached Ganzhou, news of Han Shen's murder had arrived; the court did not punish them, merely instructing them to tell their master to return seized Ming territory.

sentences.zh: 番贼知中国易与，不奉命，复遣使来贡。

translations.literal: The foreign bandits knew China was easy to deal with; they disobeyed orders and again dispatched envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Turpan's leaders, sensing the court was pliant, ignored the command and sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 礼官议薄其赏，拘使臣，番贼稍惧。

translations.literal: Ritual officials proposed reducing their rewards and detaining the envoys; the foreign bandits were somewhat afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites recommended curtailing rewards and detaining the envoys; Turpan grew somewhat fearful.

sentences.zh: 三年春，偕撒马儿罕贡狮子，愿献还城印，朝廷亦还其使臣。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, together with Samarkand they presented lions in tribute, offering to return the city and seal; the court also released their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year they sent lions as tribute jointly with Samarkand, offering to return the city and seal; the court in turn released their envoys.

sentences.zh: 礼官请却勿纳，帝不从。

translations.literal: Ritual officials requested refusal and non-acceptance; the emperor did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites urged rejection of the tribute; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 及使还，命内官张芾护行，谕内阁草敕。

translations.literal: When the envoys were to return, the eunuch Zhang Fei was ordered to escort them; the Inner Cabinet was instructed to draft an edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys departed, the eunuch Zhang Fei was ordered to escort them home, and the Grand Secretariat was told to draft an edict.

sentences.zh: 阁臣刘吉等言：“阿黑麻背负天恩，杀我所立罕慎，宜遣大将直捣巢穴，灭其种类，始足雪中国之愤。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Liu Ji and others said: "Aheima has betrayed Heaven's grace, killing Han Shen whom we installed; a great general should be dispatched straight to destroy their nest and exterminate their kind—only then can China's wrath be assuaged.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Liu Ji and others wrote: "Aheima has betrayed imperial favor and murdered Han Shen, whom we enthroned. We should send a major force straight against their stronghold and destroy them utterly—only then will the empire's outrage be satisfied.

sentences.zh: 或不即讨，亦当如古帝王封玉门关，绝其贡使，犹不失大体。

translations.literal: Or if not immediately punished, it should still be as ancient emperors who sealed the Jade Gate Pass and cut off their tribute envoys—this would not fall short of proper principle.
translations.idiomatic: Failing immediate reprisal, we should at least follow the ancient precedent of sealing the Jade Gate and cutting off their tribute missions—that would still preserve our dignity.

sentences.zh: 今宠其使臣，厚加优待，又遣中使伴送，此何理哉！

translations.literal: Now to favor their envoys, treat them lavishly, and moreover dispatch palace eunuchs to escort them—what principle is this!
translations.idiomatic: Yet now we shower their envoys with favor, treat them lavishly, and send palace eunuchs to escort them home—what sense does this make!

sentences.zh: 陛下事遵成宪，乃无故召番人入大内看戏狮子，大赉御品，夸耀而出。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's affairs follow established institutions—yet without cause barbarians are summoned into the Inner Palace to watch lions perform, lavishly granted imperial goods, and go out boastfully.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty governs by established precedent—yet you summoned these foreigners into the Inner Palace to watch the lions perform, heaped imperial gifts upon them, and sent them out to parade their favor.

sentences.zh: 都下闻之，咸为骇叹，谓祖宗以来，从无此事。

translations.literal: When the capital heard of it, all were appalled, saying that since the founding ancestors there had never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: All the capital was stunned; since the founding of the dynasty, nothing like it had ever occurred.

sentences.zh: 奈何屈万乘之尊，为奇兽之玩，俾异言异服之人，杂遝清严之地。

translations.literal: How can the dignity of the Myriad Chariots be bent for the amusement of a strange beast, allowing men of foreign speech and garb to throng the pure and solemn precincts?
translations.idiomatic: Why should the Son of Heaven demean his throne for the sake of exotic beasts, letting men in foreign dress and tongue swarm the sacred inner court?

sentences.zh: 况使臣满剌土儿即罕慎外舅，忘主事仇，逆天无道。

translations.literal: Moreover the envoy Manlatu'er was Han Shen's maternal uncle—forgetting his lord and nursing enmity, defying Heaven and without the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Worse, the envoy Manlatu'er was Han Shen's uncle by marriage—he had forsaken loyalty, nursed a blood feud, and defied all decency.

sentences.zh: 而阿黑麻聚集人马，谋犯肃州，名虽奉贡，意实叵测。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Aheima gathered men and horses, plotting to attack Suzhou; though in name presenting tribute, his intent was truly unfathomable.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Aheima was massing troops to strike Suzhou; though he came in the guise of tribute, his intentions were deeply suspect.

sentences.zh: 兵部议羁其使臣，正合事宜。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War's proposal to detain their envoys was exactly suited to the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War's recommendation to detain the envoys was entirely proper.

sentences.zh: 若不停张芾之行，彼使臣还国，阿黑麻必谓中土帝王可通情希宠，大臣谋国，天子不听，其奈我何。

translations.literal: If Zhang Fei's mission is not halted, when those envoys return home Aheima will surely think the Middle Kingdom's emperor can be swayed and favors sought—the grand ministers plot for the state but the Son of Heaven will not listen; what can they do to us?
translations.idiomatic: If Zhang Fei's escort is not stopped, when those envoys return Aheima will conclude that the Ming emperor can be cultivated for favor—that though his ministers counsel wisely, the throne will not heed them, and Turpan need fear nothing.

sentences.zh: 长番贼之志，损天朝之威，莫甚于此。”

translations.literal: To strengthen the barbarian bandits' ambition and diminish the Heavenly dynasty's prestige—nothing exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing could more embolden these border raiders or more diminish imperial prestige.

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝止芾行，而问阁臣兴师、绝贡二事。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor halted Fei's mission and questioned the Grand Secretaries on raising troops and cutting off tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor halted Zhang Fei's mission and asked the Grand Secretaries about military action and severing tribute.

sentences.zh: 吉等以时势未能，但请薄其赐赉。

translations.literal: Ji and the others, citing the times and circumstances as not permitting it, only requested reducing rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji and his colleagues, deeming the times unsuitable for war, could only recommend reducing gifts.

sentences.zh: 因言饲狮日用二羊，十岁则七千二百羊矣，守狮日役校尉五十人，一岁则一万八千人矣。

translations.literal: They further said that feeding the lions daily required two sheep—in ten years that would be seven thousand two hundred sheep; guarding lions daily conscripted fifty guards—in one year that would be eighteen thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: They added that the lions consumed two sheep daily—seven thousand two hundred over ten years—and required fifty guards each day, eighteen thousand men over a year.

sentences.zh: 若绝其餧养，听其自毙，传之千载，实为美谈。

translations.literal: If feeding ceased and they were left to die naturally, transmitted for a thousand generations this would truly be a fine story.
translations.idiomatic: If we ceased feeding them and let them die naturally, the story would echo honorably through the ages.

sentences.zh: 帝不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor could not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected the advice.

sentences.zh: 秋，又遣使从海道贡狮子，朝命却之，其使乃潜诣京师。

translations.literal: In autumn, envoys were again sent by sea route to present lions; the court ordered refusal, but the envoys secretly reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn they sent envoys by sea with lions; ordered turned back at the border, they slipped through to the capital.

sentences.zh: 礼官请治沿途有司罪，仍却其使，从之。

translations.literal: Ritual officials requested punishing officials along the route and again refusing the envoys; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites called for punishing officials along the route and again rejecting the mission; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 当是时，中外乂安，大臣马文升、耿裕辈，咸知国体，于贡使多所裁损，阿黑麻稍知中国有人。

translations.literal: At this time within and without were at peace; grand ministers such as Ma Wensheng and Geng Yu all understood national propriety, curtailing tribute missions in many ways; Aheima gradually learned that China had capable men.
translations.idiomatic: By then the realm was at peace at home and abroad; statesmen such as Ma Wensheng and Geng Yu, well versed in national dignity, repeatedly scaled back Turpan's tribute privileges, and Aheima gradually learned that the Ming had men of substance.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，遣使再贡狮子，愿还金印，及所据十一城。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year envoys were again sent to present lions, offering to return the gold seal and the eleven cities held.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year they sent lions again, offering to return the gold seal and the eleven cities they held.

sentences.zh: 边臣以闻，许之，果以城印来归。

translations.literal: Frontier officials reported it; permission was granted; indeed the city and seal were returned.
translations.idiomatic: Border officials relayed the offer; the court agreed; the city and seal were duly returned.

sentences.zh: 明年封陕巴为忠顺王，纳之哈密，厚赐阿黑麻使臣，先所拘者尽释还。

translations.literal: The next year Shaba was enfeoffed as King of Loyalty and Obedience and installed in Hami; Aheima's envoys were lavishly rewarded and all previously detained were released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Shaba was enthroned as King of Loyalty and Obedience and installed at Hami; Aheima's envoys were richly rewarded and all previously detained envoys were released.

sentences.zh: 六年春，其前使二十七人还，未出境，后使三十九人犹在京师，阿黑麻复袭陷哈密，执陕巴以去。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year, twenty-seven earlier envoys returned; before leaving the border, thirty-nine later envoys were still in the capital when Aheima again launched a surprise attack on Hami, seizing Shaba and carrying him off.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year twenty-seven earlier envoys departed; before they had cleared the border, thirty-nine later envoys still lingered in the capital when Aheima again stormed Hami and carried Shaba away captive.

sentences.zh: 帝命侍郎张海等经略，优待其使，俾得进见。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Vice Minister Zhang Hai and others to conduct operations, treating their envoys favorably and allowing them audiences.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Vice Minister Zhang Hai to manage the crisis—but still treated Turpan's envoys generously and granted them audiences.

sentences.zh: 礼官耿裕等谏曰：“朝廷驭外番，宜惜大体。

translations.literal: Ritual official Geng Yu and others remonstrated: "In governing foreign barbarians, the court should preserve overall dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Yu of the Ministry of Rites remonstrated: "In dealing with foreign peoples the court must preserve its larger dignity.

sentences.zh: 番使自去年入都，久不宣召，今春三月以来，宣召至再，且赐币帛羊酒，正当谩书投入之时，小人何知，将谓朝廷恩礼视昔有加，乃畏我而然。

translations.literal: The foreign envoys entered the capital last year and long went uncalled; since the third month this spring they have been summoned twice, and were granted silks, sheep, and wine—precisely when deceitful letters were being delivered; petty men know nothing and will think court grace and ceremony exceed the past, that it is because they fear us.
translations.idiomatic: These envoys entered the capital last year and went long without summons; since the third month they have been summoned twice and given silks, sheep, and wine—just as deceptive overtures are being exchanged. Such men will conclude the court's favor has grown because Turpan now fears us.

sentences.zh: 事干国体，不可不慎。

translations.literal: This concerns national propriety and cannot be treated carelessly.
translations.idiomatic: This touches the dignity of the state and must be handled with care.

sentences.zh: 况此贼倔强无礼，久蓄不庭之心。

translations.literal: Moreover this bandit is obstinate and without ritual; he has long harbored a rebellious heart.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover this rebel is truculent and insolent, long disloyal in heart.

sentences.zh: 所遣使臣，必其亲信腹心，乃令出入禁掖，略无防闲。

translations.literal: The envoys he dispatches must be his trusted inner circle—yet they are allowed to enter and leave the forbidden inner quarters with scarcely any guard.
translations.idiomatic: His envoys are surely his closest confidants—yet they are permitted to move freely in the imperial precincts with scarcely any restraint.

sentences.zh: 万一奸宄窥伺，潜逞逆谋，虽悔何及。

translations.literal: If by chance evil-doers spy and secretly carry out treacherous designs, even regret would come too late.
translations.idiomatic: Should assassins or conspirators seize the chance, it would be too late for regret.

sentences.zh: 今其使写亦满速儿等宴赉已竣，犹不肯行，曰恐朝廷复宣召。

translations.literal: Now envoys such as Xieyimansu'er have finished their banquets and gifts yet still refuse to depart, saying they fear the court will summon them again.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys such as Xieyimansu'er, their feasts and gifts complete, still refuse to leave, saying they fear another imperial summons.

sentences.zh: 夫不宝远物，则远人格。

translations.literal: When one does not treasure distant goods, distant people submit.
translations.idiomatic: "He who does not cherish exotic goods from afar will win submission from afar."

sentences.zh: 狮本野兽，不足为奇，何至上烦銮舆，屡加临视，致荒徼小丑，得觐圣颜，藉为口实。”

translations.literal: Lions are merely wild beasts, nothing marvelous—why trouble the imperial carriage repeatedly to view them, allowing petty men of remote frontiers to behold the sage countenance and make it a topic of boast?
translations.idiomatic: Lions are merely wild beasts, nothing to marvel at—why should the emperor repeatedly go to see them, letting petty frontier chieftains gaze upon the imperial face and brag of the honor?

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝即遣还。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor immediately ordered them sent back.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor at once ordered the envoys dismissed.

sentences.zh: 张海等抵甘肃，遵朝议，却其贡物，羁前后使臣一百七十二人于边，闭嘉峪关，永绝贡道。

translations.literal: Zhang Hai and others reached Gansu, following court deliberations refused their tribute goods, detained one hundred seventy-two envoys from earlier and later missions at the frontier, closed Jiayu Pass, and permanently cut off the tribute route.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hai reached Gansu, rejected their tribute as the court had ordered, detained all 172 envoys at the frontier, closed Jiayu Pass, and permanently severed the tribute route.

sentences.zh: 而巡抚许进等，又潜兵直捣哈密，走牙兰，阿黑麻渐惧。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Grand Coordinator Xu Jin and others also secretly led troops straight against Hami, driving off Yalan; Aheima gradually grew afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Grand Coordinator Xu Jin led a covert strike against Hami, driving off Yalan; Aheima grew increasingly fearful.

sentences.zh: 其邻邦不获贡，胥怨阿黑麻。

translations.literal: Neighboring states unable to send tribute all resented Aheima.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring states, barred from the tribute route, all blamed Aheima.

sentences.zh: 十年冬，送还陕巴，款关求贡，廷议许之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the tenth year Shaba was sent back; they knocked at the pass seeking tribute; court deliberation permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the tenth year they returned Shaba, came to the pass seeking renewed tribute, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 十二年，其使再求，命前使安置广东者悉释还。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year their envoys again petitioned; those envoys previously detained in Guangdong were all released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year they petitioned again; all envoys previously held in Guangdong were released.

sentences.zh: 十七年，阿黑麻死，诸子争立，相仇杀。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Aheima died; his sons fought over succession, mutually killing in enmity.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Aheima died; his sons fought over the succession and slaughtered one another.

sentences.zh: 已而长子满速儿嗣为速檀，修贡如故。

translations.literal: Before long the eldest son Mansu'er succeeded as sultan and continued tribute as before.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually his eldest son Mansu'er succeeded as sultan and resumed tribute as before.

sentences.zh: 明年，忠顺王陕巴卒，子拜牙即袭，昏愚失道，国内益乱。

translations.literal: The next year the King of Loyalty and Obedience Shaba died; his son Baiya immediately succeeded—foolish and lost from the Way, the state grew ever more chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: The following year King Shaba of Loyalty and Obedience died; his son Baiya succeeded at once—a dull, dissolute ruler under whom Hami descended further into chaos.

sentences.zh: 而满速儿桀黠变诈逾于父，复有吞哈密之志。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Mansu'er was cunning and deceitful beyond his father, and again harbored ambition to swallow Hami.
translations.idiomatic: Mansu'er, more cunning and treacherous than his father, again coveted Hami.

sentences.zh: 正德四年，其弟真帖木儿在甘州，贡使乞放还。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengde his younger brother Zhentiemuer was at Ganzhou; tribute envoys begged for his release and return.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 4 (1509), his younger brother Zhentiemuer was held at Ganzhou; Turpan's envoys petitioned for his release.

sentences.zh: 朝议不许，乃以甘州守臣奏送还。

translations.literal: Court deliberation did not permit it; then on petition of the defending official at Ganzhou he was sent back.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused, but the defending officer at Ganzhou petitioned and had him sent back.

sentences.zh: 还即以边情告其兄，共谋为逆。

translations.literal: On returning he immediately reported frontier conditions to his elder brother, and together they plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Once home, he at once told his brother what he had learned of frontier affairs, and together they plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 九年诱拜牙即叛，复据哈密。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he lured Baiya, who immediately rebelled, and again occupied Hami.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he enticed Baiya into revolt; Baiya at once turned traitor and Hami was seized again.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣彭泽经略，赎还城印。

translations.literal: The court dispatched Peng Ze to oversee the region and ransomed back the city seal.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Peng Ze to handle frontier affairs and bought back Hami's city and official seal.

sentences.zh: 其部下他只丁复据之，且导满速儿犯肃州。

translations.literal: His subordinate Taziding again occupied it, and moreover guided Mansu'er in an incursion against Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His follower Taziding seized Hami again and guided Mansu'er in a raid on Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 自是，哈密不可复得，而患且中于甘肃。

translations.literal: From then on Hami could not be recovered, and calamity moreover struck at Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: After this Hami was lost for good, and the threat moved deep into Gansu.

sentences.zh: 会中朝大臣自相倾陷，番酋觇知之，益肆谗构，贼腹心得侍天子，中国体大亏，贼气焰益盛。

translations.literal: Just then ministers of the central court mutually undermined one another; the barbarian chief observed this and all the more freely spread slander and intrigue; the rebel's confidant gained access to serve the Son of Heaven; the dignity of China suffered great loss; the rebels' arrogance grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time court ministers were tearing one another down. The Turpan chief saw his opening and redoubled his intrigues; Mansu'er's agent won access to the emperor's ear; China's standing was gravely diminished; and the rebels grew bolder still.

sentences.zh: 十五年复许通贡。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year tribute was again permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the court again allowed tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 甘肃巡按潘仿言：“番贼犯顺，杀戮摽掠，惨不可胜言。

translations.literal: Gansu touring censor Pan Fang said: "The barbarian bandits rebelled against obedience; killing, slaughtering, and raiding—too horrific to tell in full.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu touring censor Pan Fang wrote: "These frontier rebels have repeatedly risen against us—killing, pillaging, and laying waste beyond description.

sentences.zh: 今虽悔罪，果足赎前日万一乎？

translations.literal: Now although they repent their crimes, can it truly redeem so much as one ten-thousandth of what went before?
translations.idiomatic: Even if they now profess repentance, can that truly atone for even a fraction of what they have done?

sentences.zh: 数年以来，虽尝闭关，未能问罪。

translations.literal: For several years, although the passes were once closed, we were unable to demand accountability for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: For years we closed the passes, yet never held them to account.

sentences.zh: 今彼以困惫求通，且将窥我意向，探我虚实，缓我后图，诱我重利。

translations.literal: Now they seek contact from exhaustion and distress, and will moreover spy out our intentions, probe our strength and weakness, slow our later plans, and entice us with great profit.
translations.idiomatic: They come now because they are weary and broken—but they will watch our intentions, test our defenses, buy time for their next move, and bait us with promises of profit.

sentences.zh: 不于此时稍正其罪，将益启轻慢之心，招反覆之衅，非所以尊中国驭外番也。

translations.literal: If at this time we do not somewhat rectify their crimes, we will all the more awaken a heart of contempt, invite the provocation of repeated treachery—this is not the way to uphold China and govern outer barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not impose some reckoning now, we will only encourage their contempt and invite further treachery. That is no way for China to command the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 况彼番文执难从之词，示敢拒之状，当悔罪求通之日，为侮慢不恭之语，其变诈已见。

translations.literal: Moreover their barbarian document clutches difficult-to-follow words and displays an appearance of daring to refuse; on the very day they repent crimes and seek contact they speak insultingly and without respect—their shifting deceit is already visible.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover their memorial clings to intractable language and barely disguises defiance; even as they plead repentance they speak with insolent disrespect. Their duplicity is plain.

sentences.zh: 若曰来者不拒，驭戎之常，尽略彼事之非，纳求和之使，必将叨冒恩礼，饱餍赏饩，和市私贩，满载而归。

translations.literal: If one says those who come are not refused and governing barbarians is routine, wholly overlooking their wrongdoing and accepting peace-seeking envoys—they will surely presume upon grace and ritual, fully sated with rewards and rations, trade at market and private trafficking, and return loaded down.
translations.idiomatic: To say we must never turn away supplicants is one thing; but if we ignore their past crimes and welcome their envoys, they will drain our courtesies and rewards, trade at the markets, smuggle as they please, and go home laden with profit.

sentences.zh: 所欲既足，骄志复萌，少不慊心，动则藉口，反复之衅，且在目前。

translations.literal: Once desires are satisfied, proud intent springs up again; the slightest dissatisfaction gives cause for complaint; the provocation of repeated treachery is even now before us.
translations.idiomatic: Once they have had their fill, pride will return; the least disappointment will become their excuse—and the next betrayal is already at hand.

sentences.zh: 叛则未尝加罪，而反获钞掠之利，来则未必见拒，而更有赐赉之荣，何惮不为。

translations.literal: If they rebel they go unpunished and instead reap the profit of pillage; if they come they need not fear refusal and moreover gain the honor of gifts and bestowals—what is there to deter them from doing so?
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion brings no punishment, only the spoils of raid; submission brings gifts and honor. Why should they not do both?

sentences.zh: 臣谓宜乘窘迫之时，聊为慑伏之计，虽纳其悔过之词，姑阻其来贡之使，降敕责其犯顺，仍索归还未尽之人。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that we should seize this moment of distress as a temporary plan to intimidate and subdue them: though accepting their words of repentance, for now block their tribute envoys, issue an edict reproaching their rebellion, and still demand the return of persons not yet restored.
translations.idiomatic: I propose we use their present weakness to frighten them into compliance: accept their words of contrition in form only, block their envoys for now, send an edict condemning their rebellion, and demand the return of every captive still held.

sentences.zh: 其番文可疑者，详加诘问，使彼知中国尊严，天威难犯，庶几反侧不萌，归服可久。”

translations.literal: Where their barbarian document is suspicious, question them closely in detail, so they know China's dignity and that imperial majesty may not be violated—then perhaps wavering will not arise and submission may long endure."
translations.idiomatic: Interrogate them closely wherever their memorials seem suspect, that they may learn the majesty of China and the cost of crossing Heaven's wrath—so that they may submit in earnest and stay at peace.

sentences.zh: 时王琼力主款议，不纳其言。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Qiong strongly advocated conciliation and did not accept his words.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiong vigorously pushed for accommodation, and the court ignored Pan's advice.

sentences.zh: 明年，世宗立，贼腹心写亦虎仙伏诛，失所恃，再谋犯边。

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Shizong ascended; the rebel confidant Xieyihuxian was executed; having lost his support, he again plotted to invade the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Jiajing emperor took the throne; Mansu'er's agent Xieyihuxian was executed; stripped of his patron at court, Mansu'er again plotted border raids.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年寇肃州，掠甘州，四年复寇肃州，皆失利去，于是卑词求贡。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing they raided Suzhou and plundered Ganzhou; in the fourth year they again raided Suzhou, all withdrew after defeat, and then with humble words sought tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 3 they raided Suzhou and plundered Ganzhou; in Jiajing 4 they attacked Suzhou again, but both campaigns failed. Then they sued for tribute in submissive tones.

sentences.zh: 会璁、萼等起封疆之狱，遂阴庇满速儿再许之贡，议已定。

translations.literal: Just then Zhang Ao, Gui E, and others raised the border-affairs case; thus they secretly shielded Mansu'er and again permitted his tribute—the decision was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Zhang Ao, Gui E, and their allies opened the border-affairs prosecutions and quietly secured renewed tribute for Mansu'er; the matter was decided.

sentences.zh: 贼党牙兰者，本曲先人，幼为番掠，长而黠健，阿力以妹妻之，握兵用事，久为西陲患，至是获罪其主，七年夏，率所部二千人来降。

translations.literal: Among the rebel faction was Yalan, originally of the Qu clan; as a child he was seized by barbarians; grown he was cunning and strong; Ali gave him his sister in marriage; he wielded troops and held power; for long he was a scourge of the western frontier; at this time having offended his lord, in the summer of the seventh year he led two thousand of his followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: One of Mansu'er's men was Yalan, a Qu clansman seized by Turpan raiders as a boy and raised to be clever and fierce. Ali gave him his sister in marriage; he took command and for years plagued the western frontier. Having fallen out with his master, in the summer of the seventh year he led two thousand followers to defect.

sentences.zh: 有帖木儿哥、土巴者，俱沙州番族，土鲁番役属之，岁徵妇女牛马，不胜侵暴，亦率其族属数千帐来归。

translations.literal: There were Tiemuerge and Tuba, both of the Shazhou barbarian tribes; Turpan made them subject and yearly levied women, cattle, and horses; unable to bear the oppression and violence, they too led several thousand tents of their clansmen to come over.
translations.idiomatic: Tiemuerge and Tuba, chieftains of Shazhou tribes subordinated to Turpan, could no longer endure the annual levies of women, cattle, and horses. They too led several thousand families to the Ming side.

sentences.zh: 边臣悉处之内地。

translations.literal: Frontier officials altogether settled them within the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials resettled them all in the interior.

sentences.zh: 满速儿怒，使其部下虎力纳咱儿引瓦剌寇肃州，不胜，则复遣使求贡。

translations.literal: Mansu'er was enraged; he had his subordinate Hulinazaer lead Oirats to raid Suzhou; after defeat, he again dispatched envoys seeking tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Mansu'er sent his follower Hulinazaer to lead Oirat raiders against Suzhou. When that failed, he again sent envoys suing for tribute.

sentences.zh: 总督王琼请许之，詹事霍韬言：“番人攻陷哈密以来，议者或请通贡，或请绝贡，圣谕必有悔罪番文然后许。

translations.literal: Governor-general Wang Qiong asked that it be permitted; Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent Huo Tao said: "Since the barbarians captured Hami, some in deliberation have urged allowing tribute, others cutting it off; the holy edict requires a document of repentance before permission.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Wang Qiong recommended acceptance. Junior Mentor Huo Tao objected: "Since Turpan took Hami, some have argued for resuming tribute and others for cutting it off. The emperor ruled that tribute may resume only when a proper memorial of repentance is received.

sentences.zh: 今王琼译进之文，皆其部下小丑之语，无印信足凭。

translations.literal: Now the document Wang Qiong has translated and submitted consists entirely of words from petty underlings—no seal or credential on which to rely.
translations.idiomatic: The document Wang Qiong has submitted is the work of petty subordinates, bearing no seal or credential we can trust.

sentences.zh: 我遽许之，恐戎心益骄，后难驾驭。

translations.literal: If we hastily permit it, I fear the barbarians' hearts will grow prouder and be hard to control afterward.
translations.idiomatic: If we yield at once, the frontier peoples will only grow bolder and harder to restrain.

sentences.zh: 可虞者一。

translations.literal: That which is to be feared—the first.
translations.idiomatic: First concern:

sentences.zh: 哈密城池虽称献还，然无实据，何以兴复。

translations.literal: Although Hami's city and walls are said to have been returned, there is no solid proof—how can it be restored?
translations.idiomatic: Turpan claims to have returned Hami's city and walls, but offers no proof—how can Hami be restored?

sentences.zh: 或者遂有弃置不问之议，彼愈得志，必且劫我罕东，诱我赤斤，掠我瓜、沙，外连瓦剌，内扰河西，而边警无时息矣。

translations.literal: Some then raise the proposal of abandoning it without inquiry; the more they succeed, the more surely they will raid our Handong, entice our Chijin, plunder our Guazhou and Shazhou; join outwardly with Oirats and disturb inwardly the Hexi corridor—and frontier alarms will never cease.
translations.idiomatic: Some will say to abandon Hami entirely. Emboldened, Turpan will raid Handong, win over Chijin, plunder Guazhou and Shazhou, ally with the Oirats without and stir trouble in the Hexi corridor within—and the frontier will never know peace.

sentences.zh: 可虞者二。

translations.literal: That which is to be feared—the second.
translations.idiomatic: Second concern:

sentences.zh: 牙兰为番酋腹心，拥众来奔，而彼云不知所向，安知非诈降以诱我。

translations.literal: Yalan was the barbarian chief's trusted confidant; he came over with a following, yet they say they do not know where he went—how do we know this is not a feigned surrender to lure us?
translations.idiomatic: Yalan was Mansu'er's trusted lieutenant; he defected at the head of a host, yet Turpan claims not to know where he went. Who is to say this is not a ruse?

sentences.zh: 他日犯边，曰纳我叛臣也。

translations.literal: Another day if they invade the frontier they will say: you harbored our rebel minister.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when they raid the frontier, they will declare that we harbored their defector.

sentences.zh: 我不归彼叛臣，彼不归我哈密。

translations.literal: If we do not return their rebel minister, they will not return our Hami.
translations.idiomatic: If we keep Yalan, they will keep Hami.

sentences.zh: 自是西陲益多事，而哈密终无兴复之期。

translations.literal: From then on the western frontier would grow ever more troubled, and Hami in the end would have no day of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The western frontier would only grow more volatile, and Hami would never be restored.

sentences.zh: 可虞者三。

translations.literal: That which is to be feared—the third.
translations.idiomatic: Third concern:

sentences.zh: 牙兰之来，日给廪饩，所费实多，犹曰羁縻之策不获已也。

translations.literal: With Yalan's coming, daily grain and provisions are supplied; the cost is truly great; still one says the policy of loose reins was unavoidable.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yalan's arrival we have fed his followers daily at great expense—yet we call this unavoidable appeasement.

sentences.zh: 倘番酋拥众叩关，索彼叛人，将予之耶，抑拒之耶？

translations.literal: If the barbarian chief comes with a host to knock at the pass and demand those rebels, shall we give them or refuse them?
translations.idiomatic: If Mansu'er comes to the pass at the head of an army demanding their return, do we surrender them or refuse?

sentences.zh: 又或牙兰包藏祸心，构变于内，内外协应，何以御之？

translations.literal: Or again Yalan may harbor treacherous intent and raise trouble within, coordinating inside and outside—how are we to resist?
translations.idiomatic: Or Yalan himself may plot treachery within while Mansu'er strikes from without—how then do we defend?

sentences.zh: 可虞者四。

translations.literal: That which is to be feared—the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth concern:

sentences.zh: 或曰今陕西饥困，甘肃孤危，哈密可弃也。

translations.literal: Some say Shaanxi is now famine-stricken and distressed, Gansu isolated and perilous—Hami may be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that with Shaanxi starving and Gansu exposed, Hami should be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 臣则曰，保哈密所以保甘、陕也，保甘肃所以保陕西也。

translations.literal: Your servant says: preserving Hami is how we preserve Gan and Shaan; preserving Gansu is how we preserve Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: I say: to hold Hami is to hold Ganzhou and Shaanxi; to hold Gansu is to hold Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 若以哈密难守即弃哈密，然则甘肃难守亦弃甘肃乎？

translations.literal: If because Hami is hard to hold we abandon Hami, then if Gansu is hard to hold shall we also abandon Gansu?
translations.idiomatic: If we abandon Hami because it is hard to defend, shall we abandon Gansu when that too proves difficult?

sentences.zh: 昔文皇之立哈密也，因元遗孽力能自立，因而立之。

translations.literal: In former times when the literary emperor established Hami, it was because Yuan remnant scions could stand on their own strength, and so he established them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle emperor first established Hami, he did so because Yuan loyalists there could still hold their own—and he made use of them.

sentences.zh: 彼假其名，我享其利。

translations.literal: They borrowed the name; we enjoyed the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: They lent us the name; we reaped the profit.

sentences.zh: 今忠顺之嗣三绝矣，天之所废，孰能兴之？

translations.literal: Now the loyal-and-obedient line is thrice extinguished—what Heaven has cast off, who can raise up?
translations.idiomatic: The loyal-and-obedient line is now extinct three times over. What Heaven has abandoned, who can restore?

sentences.zh: 今于诸夷中，求其雄杰能守哈密者，即畀金印，俾和辑诸番，为我籓蔽，斯可矣，必求忠顺之裔而立焉，多见其固也。”

translations.literal: Now among all the tribes, seek one who is heroic and able to hold Hami, give him the gold seal at once, let him harmonize the various tribes and serve as our fence and screen—that suffices. Insisting on raising a descendant of Loyalty and Obedience shows only obstinacy."
translations.idiomatic: Find among the tribes a strongman capable of holding Hami, invest him with the gold seal, and let him pacify the frontier peoples as our buffer—that is enough. To insist on a descendant of the loyal-and-obedient house is mere stubbornness.

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝嘉其留心边计，下兵部确议。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor praised his attention to frontier planning and sent it to the Ministry of War for thorough deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor praised Huo Tao's concern for frontier affairs and referred it to the Ministry of War for a formal ruling.

sentences.zh: 尚书胡世宁等力言牙兰不可弃，哈密不必兴复，请专图自治之策，帝深纳其言。

translations.literal: Minister Hu Shining and others forcefully argued Yalan must not be abandoned, Hami need not be restored, and urged concentrating on a policy of self-governance—the emperor deeply accepted their view.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Hu Shining and his colleagues argued that Yalan must be kept, Hami need not be restored, and the court should focus on securing its own borders. The emperor embraced their advice.

sentences.zh: 自是番酋许通贡，而哈密城印及忠顺王存亡置不复问，河西稍获休息，而满速儿桀傲益甚矣。

translations.literal: From then on the barbarian chief was permitted tribute, while Hami's city seal and whether the King of Loyalty and Obedience lived or died were set aside and no longer questioned; the Hexi corridor briefly gained respite, while Mansu'er grew ever more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Turpan was allowed tribute again, while Hami's city seal and the fate of the loyal-and-obedient king were dropped from concern. The Hexi corridor enjoyed a brief calm—but Mansu'er grew ever more insolent.

sentences.zh: 十二年遣臣奏三事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he dispatched a minister memorializing on three matters.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he sent an envoy memorializing on three points.

sentences.zh: 一，请追治巡抚陈九畴罪。

translations.literal: First: requesting that Grand Coordinator Chen Jiuchou's crime be investigated and punished.
translations.idiomatic: First, that Grand Coordinator Chen Jiuchou be prosecuted for his offenses.

sentences.zh: 一，请遣官议和。

translations.literal: Second: requesting that officials be dispatched to negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: Second, that officials be sent to negotiate peace.

sentences.zh: 一，请还叛人牙兰。

translations.literal: Third: requesting the return of the rebel Yalan.
translations.idiomatic: Third, that the defector Yalan be returned.

sentences.zh: 词多悖慢，朝廷不能罪，但戒以修职贡无妄言。

translations.literal: The language was largely insolent and disrespectful; the court could not punish him, but only admonished him to maintain tribute duties and speak no reckless words.
translations.idiomatic: The language was brazenly insolent; the court could not punish him, but warned him to keep to his tribute duties and speak no reckless words.

sentences.zh: 然自写亦虎仙诛，他只丁阵殁，牙兰又降，失其所倚赖，势亦渐孤，部下各自雄长，称王入贡者多至十五人，政权亦不一。

translations.literal: Yet since Xieyihuxian was executed, Taziding died in battle, and Yalan again defected, he lost his reliance; his position gradually grew isolated; subordinates each became local strongmen on their own; those styling themselves kings and sending tribute reached as many as fifteen, and political authority was likewise not unified.
translations.idiomatic: Yet with Xieyihuxian executed, Taziding dead in battle, and Yalan gone over to the Ming, Mansu'er lost his pillars of support. He grew increasingly isolated; his subordinates each ruled as petty kings; as many as fifteen styled themselves sultans and sent tribute, and authority in Turpan was fractured.

sentences.zh: 十五年，甘肃巡抚赵载陈边事，言：“番酋屡服屡叛，我抚之太厚，信之太深，愈长其奸狡。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Gansu grand coordinator Zhao Zai memorialized on frontier affairs, saying: "The barbarian chief has repeatedly submitted and repeatedly rebelled; we have indulged him too richly and trusted him too deeply, ever nurturing his cunning deceit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Grand Coordinator Zhao Zai of Gansu memorialized on frontier affairs: "The Turpan chief has submitted and rebelled again and again. We have indulged him too generously and trusted him too far, only feeding his cunning.

sentences.zh: 今后入犯，宜戮其使臣，徙其从人于两粤，闭关拒绝。

translations.literal: Henceforward on incursion, tribute envoys should be executed, their followers relocated to the Two Guangs, and the passes closed in refusal.
translations.idiomatic: When they raid again, their envoys should be executed, their attendants sent to the Two Guangs, and the passes shut.

sentences.zh: 即彼悔罪，亦但许奉贡，不得辄还从人。

translations.literal: Even if they repent their crimes, only tribute missions may be allowed—the followers must not be promptly returned.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they repent, only tribute missions should be admitted—their attendants must not be sent home at once.

sentences.zh: 彼内有所牵，外有所畏，自不敢轻犯。”

translations.literal: With matters at home holding them back and fear abroad restraining them, they will not lightly offend."
translations.idiomatic: With hostages at home and fear abroad, they will not dare raid lightly.

sentences.zh: 帝颇采其言。

translations.literal: The emperor largely adopted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，满速儿死，长子沙嗣为速檀，其弟马黑麻亦称速檀，分据哈密。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Mansu'er died; his eldest son Sha succeeded as sultan; his younger brother Maheimma also styled himself sultan—they divided Hami between them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year Mansu'er died. His eldest son Sha succeeded as sultan; his younger brother Maheimma also claimed the title, and the two divided Hami between them.

sentences.zh: 已而兄弟仇杀，马黑麻乃结婚瓦剌以抗其兄，且垦田沙州，谋入犯。

translations.literal: Before long the brothers feuded and killed; Maheimma then allied by marriage with the Oirats to resist his elder brother, and moreover opened farmland at Shazhou, plotting incursion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the brothers turned on each other. Maheimma allied with the Oirats by marriage to oppose his elder brother, opened fields at Shazhou, and plotted raids.

sentences.zh: 其部下来告，马黑麻乃叩关求贡，复求内地安置。

translations.literal: His subordinates came to report this; Maheimma then knocked at the pass seeking tribute, again requesting settlement in the interior.
translations.idiomatic: When his followers reported this to the Ming, Maheimma came to the pass suing for tribute and again asked to be resettled inland.

sentences.zh: 边臣谕止之，乃还故土，与兄同处。

translations.literal: Frontier officials instructed and stopped him; he then returned to his native land and dwelt together with his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials dissuaded him; he returned to his homeland and lived alongside his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 总督张珩以闻，诏许其入贡。

translations.literal: Governor-general Zhang Heng reported this; an edict permitted his tribute mission.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Zhang Heng reported the matter; the court authorized his tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 二十六年定令五岁一贡。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year it was fixed by decree that tribute would come once every five years.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year a decree fixed tribute at once every five years.

sentences.zh: 其后贡期如令，而来使益多。

translations.literal: Thereafter the tribute schedule followed the decree, but envoys grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the tribute schedule held, but the number of envoys steadily increased.

sentences.zh: 逮世宗末年，番文至二百四十八道。

translations.literal: By the end of Shizong's reign, barbarian documents reached two hundred forty-eight in number.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Jiajing reign, Turpan memorials numbered two hundred forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 朝廷重违其情，咸为给赐。

translations.literal: The court, loath to go against their wishes, bestowed gifts upon all.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to refuse them, the court granted rewards to every mission.

sentences.zh: 隆庆四年，马黑麻嗣兄职，遣使谢恩。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Longqing Maheimma succeeded his brother's office and dispatched envoys to express gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 4 Maheimma succeeded his brother and sent envoys to offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 其弟琐非等三人，亦各称速檀，遣使来贡。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Suofei and three others also each styled themselves sultan and dispatched envoys bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Suofei and two others also styled themselves sultans and sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 礼官请裁其犒赐，许附马黑麻随从之数，可之。

translations.literal: Rites officials requested trimming their reward gifts and allowing them only as attendants counted within Maheimma's retinue; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites proposed cutting their rewards and counting them only as part of Maheimma's retinue; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 迄万历朝，奉贡不绝。

translations.literal: Down through the Wanli reign, tribute missions continued without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Wanli reign, tribute missions never ceased.
